title: How the mosquito’s carbon dioxide sense gets an internal boost
content:
by Chih-Ying Su

Mosquitoes use CO2 as a critical cue to sense if humans are nearby. A new study in PLOS Biology reveals that CO2-sensing neurons in mosquitoes can amplify each other’s signals, creating a neural echo chamber that may explain the remarkable sensitivity of mosquitoes to human presence.
